Proposition
1. ch7:7.17

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian $n$-manifold. Then \[ \operatorname {tr}_g\stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}=0, \] and the orthogonal decomposition of the Ricci tensor is egin{equation} \mathrm{Rc}=\stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}+ rac1nSg. ag {7.27} \end{equation} In the Riemannian case, egin{equation} |\mathrm{Rc}|_g^2 =|\stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}|_g^2+ rac1nS^2. ag {7.28} \end{equation}

Remark
The norm identity (7.28) uses positive definiteness. For a pseudo-Riemannian metric, the corresponding identity is \[ \langle \mathrm{Rc},\mathrm{Rc} angle _g =\left\langle \stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}, \stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}} ight angle _g+ rac1nS^2. \]

Proof

\sketch Since $\operatorname {tr}_gg=g_{ij}g^{ji}=n$, the definition gives $\operatorname {tr}_g\stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}=0$ and (7.27). For every symmetric $2$-tensor $h$,

\[ \langle h,g angle _g =g^{ik}g^{jl}h_{ij}g_{kl} =g^{ij}h_{ij} =\operatorname {tr}_gh. \]

Thus $\stackrel{\circ }{\mathrm{Rc}}$ is orthogonal to $g$. In the Riemannian case, take squared norms in (7.27) and use $\langle g,g angle _g=n$ to obtain (7.28).

□

For a smooth $2$-tensor $T$, define its exterior covariant derivative by \[ (DT)(X,Y,Z)=-( abla T)(X,Y,Z)+( abla T)(X,Z,Y). \qquad (7.29) \] In components, \[ (DT)_{ijk}=-T_{ij;k}+T_{ik;j}. \]
